90% of this code shouldn't exist.  Use the phosphor-dbus-interfaces generated client code.
Patrick, I didn't understand this, How I can use the phosphor-dbus-interfaces generated client code here?
PDI already generates dbus client code and has for like 2+ years now.
Can you please check once more, I have removed the un-necessary code.

This path is only ever going to be hosted by mctpd; why the indirection through the mapper? I suggest you rather use mctpd's bus name directly and call GetManagedObjects

Also I don't see that you're setting a match to watch for endpoints coming and going?
In mctp code construct data type for EID is uint32, we can remove uint8.
It is byte in the d-bus interfaces.https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/MCTP/Endpoint.interface.yaml#L18
Yes it was in downstream and based on the old design, But it is not required now with in kernel socket
We should be able to use type header from libspdm here.
Not in this commit, we can do it in this commit : 80267
Do you really want to fetch from the root? I expect you're only interested in endpoint devices, not other objects like interfaces and networks.
This is "sync" call. As the daemon itself is using async sdbusplus, prefer to make the whole daemon async.
This blocks. Shouldn't it be async?
Are we just doing this once? You should have a match on mctpd's object tree, and react to the coming and going of endpoints, right?
Yes but this is for only for the start up and yes the matches are also required, will bring it in later commit. these are the initial commits.
Define an alias for this complicated data.
And possibly create a "utils.cpp" to put the generic dbus call's wrappers.
The 3 functions here are more like "util" functions that is not supposed to be a member function, possibly make them static or move them to "utils" as well?
Prefer to move there constexpr values into cpp and put them in a namespace.
same as above and throughout the patch
can we rename it something better? `eidValue`
This looks better, which is already there
The `invalid_eid` concept doesn't seem right. Use `std::expected`? Or `std::optional`?
This seems ... surprising. Why do we need an in-band value? Can we not rather use `std::optional`?
This needs to be tested on an upstream Nvidia platform (B40).

why do we need UUID ? if we are dealing with overlapping eid's across multiple mctp networks why cannot we use eid & networkid ? or otherwise just use UUID alone without the EID ? Not understanding why we need both.
using std::optional<std::string> - with returning an std::nullopt is better rather than passing empty strings and having string empty checks everywhere.
doxygen throughout the entire patch set looks a little off. The spacings between the function arguments are way off making it very difficult to read. please fix this all through out the patch series.
nit: use const expr for all
same callback is moved twice, this will result in bad function call exception when error path is hit.
How come many comments have been acknowledge and marked resolved but the code hasn't changed?
Would it be possible to refactor all of these into coroutine functions? I believe that would improve readability.

What is the purpose of the interface hierarchy? If it is meant to enable extensibility to other device types, the responder info currently embeds MCTP‑specific assumptions and should be decoupled from MCTP details.
How should this handle other TCP-based devices? Do we need to modify ResponderInfo for each device type?
Can we use co_await to make the code look synchronous? make getManagedObjectsAsync a coroutine and you can drop the double-moved lambdas and nontrivial inline callbacks.
